question.prompt: Henry starts a trip when the hands of the clock are together between \(8\) a.m. and \(9\) a.m. He arrives at his destination between \(2\) p.m. and \(3\) p.m. when the hands of the clock are exactly \(180^\circ\) apart. The trip takes:

solutions.explanation:
Consider the clock exactly six hours after Henry starts. The minute hand has completed six full turns and points in its original direction. The hour hand has completed half a turn, so it points exactly opposite its original direction. Since the hands were together at departure, they are now \(180^\circ\) apart.

A departure between \(8\) a.m. and \(9\) a.m. shifts to a time between \(2\) p.m. and \(3\) p.m., as required. We must also check that there is no other possible arrival time in that hour. The minute hand gains on the hour hand at
\[
6-\frac12=\frac{11}{2}
\]
degrees per minute, giving a gain of only \(330^\circ\) in an hour. Two successive opposite positions require a full \(360^\circ\) gain, so there is at most one such position between \(2\) and \(3\).

Thus the arrival must be exactly six hours after departure. The trip takes \(\boxed{6\text{ hours}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
solutions.title: Shift forward six hours

solutions.explanation:
The minute hand moves \(360/60=6\) degrees per minute, while the hour hand moves \(30/60=1/2\) degree per minute. Thus the minute hand gains \(11/2\) degrees per minute.

At \(8\) a.m., the hour hand is \(240^\circ\) clockwise from the minute hand. If \(s\) is the number of minutes after \(8\) when they meet, then
\[
\frac{11}{2}s=240,
\qquad s=\frac{480}{11}.
\]
This lies between \(0\) and \(60\). Since the relative gain in that hour is only \(330^\circ\), this is its only coincidence.

At \(2\) p.m., the minute hand trails the hour hand by \(60^\circ\). Their separation first shrinks to zero, so the opposite position occurs after the minute hand passes the hour hand. It must gain \(60^\circ+180^\circ=240^\circ\). If \(t\) is the number of minutes after \(2\), then
\[
\frac{11}{2}t=240,
\qquad t=\frac{480}{11}.
\]
Again this is within the hour and is the only opposite position there, because another would require an additional \(360^\circ\) gain.

The departure and arrival have identical minute offsets, \(43\tfrac7{11}\) minutes after their respective hours. Their difference is therefore \(\boxed{6\text{ hours}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
solutions.title: Find the minute offsets
